title: German formations met by the Allies in northern France, 6 June to 31 August 1944

divisions.name: 6th Parachute Regiment
divisions.note: An independent regiment of the 2nd Parachute Division attached in the Cotentin: 3,457 men in fifteen companies (Harrison p. 239). The game gives it three battalions and none of the division's artillery or troops.

position0606.note: Command post north of Périers when the landings began; on 6 June the regiment moved up through Carentan to Saint-Côme-du-Mont and its 3rd Battalion returned to Carentan (Harrison pp. 297-298). Placed at Carentan, which it defended until it pulled out before dark on 11 June (Harrison p. 364).

arrive.note: In the Carentan area on D-Day

notes: Ellis lists 51 divisions; this file has the 51 names from Appendix V Part II. OCR read "8oth" as 89th and "7ooth" as 709th, the only divisions with those shapes in the 1944 West.

position0606 is the division centre at midnight 5/6 June 1944 in slice game km; page numbers come from the page headers in the OCR text of the CMH edition and may be off by one. Divisions outside the slice enter at the map edge on their arrival date.

arrive.date is the first date the source puts the division, or its first battle group, in or at the Normandy battle area; status inference marks dates Claude read from narrative wording. cite gives source and page from the running heads of the OCR text, which may be one or two pages off.
